senses.definition: A root that grows from a stem or other plant part above the soil.
senses.example: A trumpet vine uses aboveground roots to hold itself against rough bark.

senses.definition: The movement of plant seeds from one place to another by ants.
senses.example: Ant seed dispersal can move trillium seeds away from the parent plant.

senses.definition: A thin part of a plant that reaches for a nearby support or clings to it as the plant grows.
senses.example: A Virginia creeper can stick to a wall with a pad on the end of a climbing tendril.

senses.definition: A whole leaf made up of several smaller blades called leaflets on one shared stalk.
senses.example: A white clover's compound leaf usually has three leaflets.

senses.definition: A tree that makes cones, which may hold seeds or produce pollen.
senses.example: An eastern white pine is a cone-bearing tree.

senses.definition: A woody bump that grows upward from the roots of some cypress trees, especially around wet ground.
senses.example: Several cypress knees stood above the mud around the tree.

senses.definition: A leaf of a fern, often divided into many smaller parts.
senses.example: A single fern frond can look like a row of small leaves.

senses.definition: A leaf that rests on the surface of the water.
senses.example: A white water lily holds a floating leaf on a stalk connected to the plant below.

senses.definition: A leaf or leaf-like part near a flower that may look different from an ordinary leaf.
senses.example: A dogwood's bright floral bracts surround its much smaller flowers.

senses.definition: A close group of many tiny flowers that may look like one larger flower.
senses.example: The dandelion's yellow flower head contains many little flowers.

senses.definition: A group of flowers with stalks that spread from near one spot, like ribs of an umbrella.
senses.example: The small flower stalks in Queen Anne's lace make an umbel.

senses.definition: A nest built on or in a shallow spot in the ground.
senses.example: A killdeer may use stones or plant pieces around its ground nest.

senses.definition: A nest attached above itself to something like twigs so its bottom hangs free.
senses.example: A Baltimore oriole weaves a hanging nest that looks like a small bag.

senses.definition: A plant part carrying seeds or small fruits that clings to things with tiny hooks.
senses.example: The hooked bur caught in the fuzzy cloth.

senses.definition: A rounded or pointed part that sticks out along the edge of a leaf but stays joined to the rest of the blade.
senses.example: A lobe on a sassafras leaf can look like a thumb.

senses.definition: A group of leaves spreading outward from one low point on a plant.
senses.example: A dandelion's leaf rosette can spread flat on the ground.

senses.definition: The little stalk that joins most leaf blades to the rest of a plant.
senses.example: A leaf stem can carry water to a leaf as well as hold it in place.

senses.definition: A narrow part of a flower that can hold sweet nectar at its tip or along its inside.
senses.example: A hummingbird can reach into a columbine's nectar spur.

senses.definition: A group of needle-shaped leaves that grow together from a single point.
senses.example: An eastern white pine usually grows five needles in each needle bundle.

senses.definition: The hollow, rounded part of a nest where the eggs or young can sit.
senses.example: A barn swallow uses mud to shape its nest cup.

senses.definition: The exposed layers on the outside of a woody stem or trunk.
senses.example: Thin parts of a paper birch's outer bark sometimes curl back.

senses.definition: A stem that grows along the ground and can make new roots at some places it touches.
senses.example: A white clover makes rooting runners that can start new growth along the soil.

senses.definition: A tuft of hairs that slows the fall of a seed or a fruit and helps the wind carry it.
senses.example: A dandelion's seed parachute can drift out of sight on a breeze.

senses.definition: A dry fruit that holds seeds and often opens along one or more edges when ripe.
senses.example: A ripe milkweed seed pod opens to show seeds with white hairs.

senses.definition: A joint in the shell of some turtles that lets part of the shell lift or close.
senses.example: The box turtle used its shell hinge as it tucked its head away.

senses.definition: A leaf with one blade rather than separate leaflets.
senses.example: A sugar maple has a simple leaf even though the blade has deep cuts along its edge.

senses.definition: A plant with visible leaves or flowers for a short time in early spring, then a long rest below ground.
senses.example: A trout lily is a spring ephemeral that blooms before tall trees put out leaves.

senses.definition: An opening inside the trunk or a branch of a tree.
senses.example: A house wren can take small sticks into a tree cavity for a nest.
